messages:
alex: Seeing repeated burn-rate alerts for SLO /api-gen @oncall — what's the quickest place to pull traces/logs? Don't want to start rerouting until we know if it's infra or model.

jamie: Start with the SLO dashboard in Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abcd/slo-overview?orgId=1&var-slo=api-gen — the burnrate panel shows the offending window. Then open the downstream panels (errors, latency P95/P99).

alex: Nice, do I need any special perms to see traces?

maria: Traces live in Tempo (Jaeger UI proxy) — https://tracing.redwood.com/search. If you can see Grafana you usually have access. Query example in Jaeger: service="api-gen" span.operation=\"request\" and look for spikes in duration > 500ms.

jamie: For logs: Datadog logs query: `service:api-gen AND status:error` or `@http.status_code:[500 TO 599]` — https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Aapi-gen. Also check the KV cache eviction metric panel (grafana->model-cache) — lots of evictions correlate with higher CPU on hosts.

tim: FYI the burn-rate alert is currently configured as: burn_rate > 5x over 1h (SLO alert policy). If this is noisy we should consider smoothing to 2h or adding a small cooldown. I can open a PR to infra-alerts if needed.

alex: I'll run the queries now — if it's model-side we'll hit the fallback variant and throttle. If infra, we'll scale dedicated pool. Will report back in ~10m.

alex: quick questions while I'm in there — where's the runbook for SLO escalations?

maria: Runbook is in the incidents repo: https://git.internal/redwood/incidents/tree/main/slo-runbooks/api-gen.md — steps 1-4: verify, isolate, mitigate, postmortem.

jamie: If you find the error budget is being eaten by synthetic traffic, check the synthetic-tests dashboard and mute the synthetic monitor for the window (with a note).

alex: Got a few 502s from nginx + a couple model timeouts. Traces show request entering model server and timing out at 30s. Pushing fallback while we dig.

tim: Thanks — if you think it's a model perf regression, tag the RLHF team and set a short canary to the previous model. Also file an eval if outputs look off.

alex: Filed PR to infra-alerts to extend burn window to 2h + rationale: https://git.internal/redwood/infra-alerts/pull/452 — added links to dashboards and this thread.

jamie: :thumbsup: good call. Keep an eye on token throughput; if token rate is steady but latency spikes it's likely model.

alex: Update: scaled dedicated pool by +2 nodes, fallbacks in place, errors trending down. Will leave monitoring on for another 30m before closing.

sre-bot: incidentbot: alert acknowledged by alex; annotated in incident log (incident-2026-04-15-190045).

alex: closing for now, will open a postmortem if burn continues. Thanks all.
